chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Khalid ibn Ismail, from a man from our companions from the people of the mountain, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I mentioned the Magians to him, and that they say: 'Their marriage is like the marriage of the children of Adam,' and they argue against us with that. So he said: 'As for you, they should not argue against you with it. When Hibbatullah came of age, Adam said: 'O Lord, marry Hibbatullah.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down Hawa' for him, and she gave birth to him to four boys. Then Allah raised her. So when the children of Hibbatullah came of age, he said: 'O Lord, marry the children of Hibbatullah.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him that he should propose to a man from the Jinn, who was a Muslim, having four daughters for his sons. So he married them. Thus, whatever was of beauty and forbearance, it was from the Hawa' and Prophethood; and whatever was of foolishness or sharpness of temper, it was from the Jinn.'

key_terms.حَوْرَاءَ: Hawwa' (Eve), often interpreted in Shia tradition as a specific created being sent from heaven
key_terms.هِبَةُ اللَّهِ: Gift of God (a name for Adam or his son)

ai.seo_question: Why do Magians claim their marriage is like Adam's, and how does Shia theology refute or contextualize this?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the Magians' claim that their marriage customs mirror the primordial union of Adam by highlighting the unique divine intervention in human creation. He explains that while Adam was married to Hawa' (Eve) directly from heaven, his sons were married to daughters of a believing Jinn, creating a dual lineage. This distinction allows Shia scholars to attribute noble traits like prophethood and forbearance to the divine/Hawa' lineage, while attributing base traits to the Jinn lineage, thereby validating the superiority of the Ahl al-Bayt's spiritual heritage.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Khalid Bin Ismail, from a man from our companions from the people of the mountain, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>. said.

‘I mentioned the Magians to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘And they are saying that a marriage (of theirs) is like a marriage of the children of Adam<sup>as</sup>, and they are arguing against us with that’. 
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for you (Shias) all, so they should not be arguing against you with it. When Hibbatullah became an adult, Adam<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Get Hibbatullah to be married’. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sent down a Hourie for him, and she gave birth for him to four boys. Then Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Raised her (back).
So when the children of Hibbatullah became adults, he<sup>as</sup> said, ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Get the children of Hibbatullah to be married’. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup> that he<sup>as</sup> should make a proposal to a man from the Jinn, and he was a Muslim having four daughters for him, for the sons of Hibbatullah. So he married them. Thus whatever was from the beauty and the forbearance, so it is from the Hourie, along with the Prophet-hood; and whatever was from the foolishness or violent anger, so it is from the Jinn’.
en.sarwar: 58. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Khalid ibn ‘Isma’il from a man of our people of the mountains who has said the following:

“I once mentioned to abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, Zoroastrians and that they say, ‘A marriage like the marriage of the sons of Adam and that they argue with us about it. He (the Imam) said, ‘They cannot argue against you because of what Hibbahtu Allah found. Adam said, ‘O Lord, find marriage for Hibbahtu Allah.’ Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sent for him a Hawra’ who gave birth to four boys, and then Allah raised her. When sons of Hibbahtu Allah grew up he said, ‘O Allah find marriage for the sons of Hibbahtu Allah.’ Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sent him revelation to propose marriage to a man (head of the family) of Jinn who was a Muslim and had four daughters, for the sons of Hibbahtu Allah. He gave them in marriage to them. Whatever is of beauty and forbearance, it is from al-Hawra’ and whatever is of dimwittedness and temperament, is because of al-Jinn.’”
